candidates: In documentation code examples (e.g., package.json script blocks, config file snippets), verify that all entries are syntactically complete and unique: no duplicate keys, and no incomplete template tokens such as `<project-name` missing its closing `>`.

On framework-specific documentation pages, verify that all prose references to the framework name (builder, renderer, etc.) match the page's actual subject. Copy-pasting from a sibling page (e.g., adapting a Vite page for Webpack) commonly introduces incorrect framework name references that are easy to miss.

The opening sentence of the Install section in `docs/get-started/frameworks/*.mdx` pages should follow the canonical phrasing: "To install Storybook in an existing [Framework] project, run this command in your project's root directory."

When editing framework documentation pages, check for and remove any content—migration callouts, configuration notes, or version-specific guidance—that applies only to Storybook major versions that are no longer supported or relevant to current users.

When prose descriptions include a list of parallel adjectives (e.g., "faster, more stable, maintained, and better documented"), ensure all items are grammatically parallel—use compound adjectives like "well-maintained" or "actively maintained" rather than bare past participles that break the pattern.

Before merging MDX documentation that uses custom JSX components (e.g., `<SomeNewComponent>`), confirm the component is implemented and exported from the documentation site's component infrastructure. An undefined component will silently break rendering on every page that references it.

Before merging MDX documentation that references static asset paths (e.g., icon image URLs), confirm those files exist in the repository or are guaranteed to be served by the documentation build pipeline. Missing assets should be added or the paths corrected before the PR lands, and the fix should be applied consistently across all pages that share the same path pattern.
